transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (recording)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Rivera (Crestview CTO), Evan Liu (ML Engineer), Priya Kapoor (Platform Lead), Oliver Kane (SRE), Lina Gomez (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Quick demo of Optimize console and quant profiles. Focus on how SLA requirements map to precision choices, fallback rules, and cost/latency trade-offs. Action items: sandbox access, pricing, prompt sets.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, I run the AE for this region. Um quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta: Marta here, hi.
[00:08] Evan: Evan on the line.
[00:10] Priya: Priya here.
[00:12] Oliver: Oliver.
[00:13] Lina: Lina.
[00:15] Jia: Jia Chen, Redwood SE, hi all.
[00:17] Samir: Great. Our goal today is to walk through Optimize — specifically building precision or quant profiles that match an SLA-driven latency budget, show how the console shows expected quality delta between INT8 and FP8, and how fallbacks work. We'll leave 10 minutes for Q&A and next steps.
[00:35] Marta: Sounds good, we gave the doc you sent a skim. We're primarily concerned about average P95 latency under 250ms for our chat assist, and also can't degrade accuracy by more than ~3% on our classification prompts.
[00:48] Samir: Perfect. That's exactly the constraints we'll map in the demo. Jia, do you want to kick off the console?
[00:54] Jia: Yeah let's share screen. Can you see the Optimize dashboard?
[00:58] Marta: Yup.
[01:00] Jia: Okay, starting in the console, first step is "New Precision Profile". We pick target model — we're using open-llama-70b-qw for this sandbox, but this is similar for any model family. Note: transcription may say open lama.
[01:16] Evan: Quick Q — can we run this against a private Redwood deployment? We need data never leave our VPC for the pilot.
[01:22] Jia: Yes, you can run Optimize in our private mode — we have a VPC connector for the console and provisioning steps, Samir will follow up. For today's demo I have a hosted sandbox.
[01:31] Samir: Also to call out: for private installs we give the same Optimize UI but with different routing policy and no telemetry leaving your env, that's been a strong ask.
[01:40] Jia: Back to the profile — we set a latency budget (P95 <= 250ms). Console asks for traffic mix — short chat messages, medium summaries, and long-context prompts. I import a sample prompt set (you will upload your 5 canonical prompts in the sandbox later). The UI estimates tokenization distribution.
[01:58] Jia: Now Optimize shows a suite of candidate configurations: INT8 aggressive, INT8 conservative, FP8 mixed, FP8 full, hybrid bitwidth where early tokens are fp8 then switch. It shows projected P95 and quality delta against baseline FP16. Notice the quality delta column — it's an eval-derived estimate with CI.
[02:18] Oliver: How reliable are those estimates? We need to present to our compliance folks.
[02:22] Jia: They're based on Redwood's eval harness run on representative prompts. It's not perfect; there is variance. We surface confidence intervals and worst-case fallbacks. Also you can upload your own eval metrics to calibrate.
[02:34] Lina: The UI also mentions KV cash — ha, that was a transcription glitch — it's KV cache, right?
[02:39] Jia: Right KV cache. Good catch.
[02:41] Samir: Let's click the INT8 conservative candidate. Optimize simulates throughput and latency curves. See the P50/P95 slider and cost per 1k tokens. INT8 conservative keeps quality delta under 1.8% but P95 is at 220ms for the short chat mix.
[02:59] Evan: And what's the FP8 mixed?
[03:02] Jia: FP8 mixed gives P95 180ms but quality delta is 2.7% on your summary prompts in our baseline. So FP8 yields lower latency but slightly more degradation in some prompt families.
[03:12] Marta: That 2.7% — our threshold was 3% so it's borderline. How confident are we on the 2.7%?
[03:18] Jia: CI shows +/- 0.6% so there's some risk. The console flags borderline candidates in orange and suggests safety nets: automatic fallback to FP8->INT8 hybrid or automatic reroute to a higher-quality variant if a prompt fails eval.
[03:31] Samir: One important thing — Optimize can create a routing rule: if evaluation metric for a prompt family falls below threshold, it will route that request to a higher-precision model or to a dedicated pool. This is live traffic safe.
[03:43] Oliver: For our SREs, what's the cost impact if we set fallback to always prefer higher precision on failures?
[03:48] Jia: The console gives a projected delta on cost per hour depending on fail rate. If your fail rate is low (1-2%), cost bump is minimal. We also simulate worst-case 10% fail rate so you can plan.
[03:59] Lina: Can we do A/B style rollouts? Like start 10% of traffic on FP8 and monitor quality?
[04:03] Jia: Yep, rollout controls in the console let you do canaries and rollout windows, metric-based ramps, and automatic rollback.
[04:10] Marta: How does this integrate with our existing inference stack? We're on K8s and use our own model registry.
[04:15] Samir: Integration options: hosted Redwood API where you hit our endpoints; dedicated capacity where we provision GPUs in your cloud account; or private deployment inside your VPC with the same control plane. For the pilot we recommend dedicated first or private if you need no egress.
[04:29] Evan: For fidelity checks, can we run a full-sweep benchmark across our log corpus?
[04:33] Jia: Yes we can run a perf + fidelity sweep. Two options: 1) you upload prompts and baseline outputs and we run a quantitative sweep in the sandbox (fast, limited scale), 2) schedule a longer perf run in your staging infra to capture network and infra variability.
[04:46] Samir: We'll propose a 48-hour perf run in staging to get realistic numbers — that's in the next steps.
[04:52] Marta: There was also a mention in the doc about adaptive prefix caching — does that change the precision choice?
[04:58] Jia: Good question. Prefix/KV caching reduces tokens generated per request and can change the cost/latency balance. In many cases, effective caching allows more aggressive precision without hurting latency SLOs. Optimize factors in cache hit-rate assumptions when projecting costs.
[05:12] Oliver: Security — we need SOC2 logs, SSO, and KMS. How do you handle logs for private deployments?
[05:18] Samir: For private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM, logs stay in your audit cluster, and we support SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[05:26] Marta: Great. Walk us through a concrete failure scenario: a prompt family suddenly degrades in quality, what happens?
[05:31] Jia: The console shows continuous eval dashboards. If quality drops below the threshold the rule triggers and future requests matching that prompt family get routed to the safer variant. We log the events, surface traces, and can notify PagerDuty.
[05:41] Evan: Any automation to reduce false positives? We don't want frequent flips.
[05:45] Jia: Yes thresholding includes a debounce window and trend detection to avoid noisy flips. You can set the sensitivity in the rule.
[05:52] Samir: I want to demo the live fallback config — switching on a simulated degraded prompt. Jia, trigger the sim?
[05:57] Jia: Running simulation now — sending traffic mix and dropping quality on summary-family. The console highlights the drop, rule fired, and traffic rerouted to FP8-conservative variant. You can see P95 bounce up a bit on the rerouted pool.
[06:15] Lina: Nice. Anything about telemetry costs? Sending token-level traces is heavy.
[06:19] Jia: We support sampling and token-level traces can be turned off. Console shows per-token cost breakdown if you enable it. For most pilots we use sampled telemetry.
[06:29] Marta: For the pilot success criteria — we'd want P95 <= 250ms, quality delta <= 3% across all four prompt families, and no more than 3% fallback rate. Are we aligned?
[06:40] Samir: Yes, that's a concrete set. We'll record that as the pilot SLAs.
[06:44] Evan: Also need to measure cold-start tails — how does quantization affect cold KV cache fills?
[06:49] Jia: Cold starts can be worse for heavier precision because load per token increases. Optimize reports cold-start P99 and suggests instance warm pools or prefix-specific caching.
[06:57] Oliver: Deployment ops question — if we pick INT8, does Redwood manage quant kernels or does our infra need extra libs?
[07:02] Jia: For hosted/dedicated we manage kernel selection and optimizations. For private, we provide the runtime package with kernel selection scripts and a small agent; your infra team installs it on nodes. We also version the runtime.
[07:15] Marta: What about model variants? If we need to keep higher fidelity for certain classes, can we pin those to FP16 while serving rest as INT8?
[07:21] Jia: Absolutely; routing rules can pin prompt families to a specific model variant or precision. That's a common pattern.
[07:28] Samir: Quick demo of the cost calculator — enter estimated traffic, hit rate, fallback rate, and it produces monthly cost delta between configs. Shows token/hour and $/month.
[07:40] Lina: Can we export the whole plan to a spreadsheet for finance?
[07:43] Jia: Yep, export as CSV and we also have an API to pull profile configs. Samir will include the pricing template.
[07:50] Marta: Anything about rollback SLAs? If we push a profile and it causes larger issues, how fast can we revert?
[07:55] Jia: Rollbacks are immediate via the console; also you can set automatic rollback if quality metrics fall below threshold for X minutes.
[08:02] Evan: On instrumentation: what signals does Optimize use for quality? Token overlap? BLEU? Embedding-similarity?
[08:08] Jia: It supports multiple metrics — you can plug in embedding-sim, exact-match, custom ML eval functions, or our out-of-box classifiers. We recommend a combination for robust detection.
[08:20] Marta: Okay let's talk timeline — we're aiming for a pilot starting 2026-11-17. Is that feasible?
[08:27] Samir: Yes. Jia?
[08:28] Jia: We need prompts and baseline outputs by 2026-11-12, then we'll provision sandbox and run an initial 48-hour sweep the week of 11/16.
[08:35] Samir: I'll send the pricing and the pilot spreadsheet today, and Jia will share console access.
[08:40] Lina: Can we get a short recording of today's demo for the execs?
[08:42] Samir: Recording will be shared.
[08:44] Marta: Quick legal note — we'll need a paperless data processing addendum for the pilot.
[08:48] Samir: Noted, legal pack in followup.
[08:50] (crosstalk)
[09:05] Samir: Alright any final Qs?
[09:08] Evan: One more — in the console example you used open-llama-70b-qw. For our models that are homegrown, does Optimize support custom model binaries?
[09:17] Jia: Yes, you can bring-your-own-model. We support model packaging and runtime ingestion; we just need the model artifact and a small adapter. There are size/format constraints we will share.
[09:28] Oliver: For the staging perf run, what's the expected infra footprint?
[09:32] Jia: We'll produce an infra sizing estimate in the perf template — typically a handful of GPUs for realistic load, depending on concurrency.
[09:40] Samir: Okay let's recap real quick: 1) Samir sends pilot pricing and spreadsheet, 2) Jia provisions sandbox and invites Crestview, 3) Crestview provides 5 prompt families + baselines, 4) run 48-hour sweep week of 11/16, 5) security/legal docs delivered.
[09:57] Marta: That's good.
[10:00] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf run and a separate legal/security sync.
[10:09] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Some proper nouns and acronyms may be transcribed incorrectly (open-llama vs OpenLLaMA, KV cash vs KV cache); filler words and brief crosstalk present.
